args.summary:
Modelled a 10-span (10×25 m) precast small-box girder bridge made continuous, as a 2D spine beam (structure.idealization=spine_beam_2d, system=continuous — no pier column geometry given, so bearings on rigid supports).

- Section: integrated midspan small-box geometry → single girder A=1.0605 m², I=0.25166 m⁴; 4 girders combined → A=4.2421 m², I=1.00663 m⁴. C50: Ec=34500 MPa; prestressed concrete γ=26 kN/m³ → w=110.29 kN/m (self-weight of main girders only).
- Bearings: 300×350 mm, 4 internal layers of 8 mm (te=0.032 m), 8 per line (2 per girder end × 4). Sliding supports at 0–4, 7–10 use PTFE sliding (longitudinal free, Kh=0); fixed plain elastomeric at Piers 5 and 6 (longitudinal spring Kh=26250 kN/m). All: vertical spring Kv=11.33×10⁶ kN/m, S=10.096, rotation free.
- Live load: Highway Class I, 3 lanes (one-way 11.5 m), ξ=0.78, qk=10.5 kN/m, Pk=310 kN per span (L0=25 m), impact μ=0.2467 from modal f1=4.4148 Hz.
- Model ran cleanly: first three vertical frequencies 4.41/4.54/4.88 Hz; self-weight reactions and lane-load moments (max +6410 kN·m, max −4601 kN·m) computed.
